title: AlphaFold 3-guided mutagenesis identifies a candidate substrate-orienting enzyme residue
summary: For an enzyme studied in a plant natural-product pathway, the authors used an AlphaFold 3 structure model with substrate docking and molecular-dynamics analysis to nominate candidate pocket residues. Mutational tests found that replacing one predicted aromatic residue abolished measured activity, while a conservative aromatic substitution restored activity, supporting a role in substrate orientation. This is a bounded residue-level mechanistic result: the authors report that the mutations do not establish a comprehensive mechanism and the predicted protein and complex structures were not experimentally characterized.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3 structure prediction with substrate docking and molecular-dynamics-guided residue selection
organization: Max Planck Institute for Chemical Ecology; University of Georgia; Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research

evidence.tested: AlphaFold 3 structure modeling, putative-substrate docking and molecular-dynamics analysis nominated candidate residues; targeted mutations directly tested their contribution to activity. One aromatic-residue substitution eliminated measured activity and a conservative aromatic substitution restored it.
evidence.unknown: The predicted protein and complex structures were not experimentally characterized; authors state the mutational analysis is not comprehensive. No independent replication is reported.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 3 structure modeling plus docking and molecular-dynamics analysis guided selection of residues for mutational testing, supporting a specific hypothesis about substrate orientation. The model was a guide to experiments, not an experimental structure or a complete mechanistic proof.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary publisher Results describing AlphaFold3-guided residue selection and mutational test, structural/mechanistic caveats, publication/version date and affiliations. No experimental reproduction.
